major.title: MAJOR 1 — `check-zeroize-chain` does not read the graph `--locked`: its own error string, the CI comment and DEPENDENCIES.md say it does, and a stale Cargo.lock is silently rewritten with a green verdict
major.detail: scripts/check-zeroize-chain.ts:62 spawns `cargo metadata --format-version 1` with no `--locked`; :67 reports 'cargo metadata --locked failed', .github/workflows/ci.yml:52-53 says the gate 'reads the resolved graph through cargo metadata --locked', DEPENDENCIES.md:34-35 says the same. Replay: with the cpubits [[package]] block deleted from Cargo.lock, `cargo metadata --locked` exits 101 while the gate exits 0 with 'Zeroize chain intact' and puts the block back (Cargo.lock rewritten, diff empty afterwards); the feature mutation left a 4-line lock rewrite behind the gate as well. Consequence for the security claim: the verdict is computed on whatever cargo resolves at that moment — with network access in the Bun job (12 s step) — not on the committed lock the Rust job builds; the two required jobs can disagree on the graph. Bounded because features come from manifests (a lock cannot turn `zeroize` off) and `Rust quality` fails `--locked` on a stale lock, so the wipe property still holds for the graph that ships; what fails is the gate's stated property and the silent-guardrail rule (a gate that says --locked and is not). Closure: add `"--locked"` (and `--offline` in CI if wanted) to the spawnSync arguments; a bun test cannot cover it (the fixture path bypasses cargo), so a comment-to-code check or a CI `git diff --exit-code Cargo.lock` after `bun run check` would hold the line.

The zeroize-chain gate's verdict is computed on cargo's live resolution, not the committed lock, until `--locked` is added (MAJOR 1); the wipe property itself was proven red/green by mutation on both the compile-time assertion and the gate.

Coverage boundary of the two wipe gates, stated: the compile assertion binds `Aes256Gcm` and `aes::Aes256` to `ZeroizeOnDrop` (member drops: aes Drop -> zeroize_flat_type; Polyval Drop -> zeroize_flat_type; temporary ghash key zeroized); the script binds the `zeroize` feature and uniqueness of aes/ghash/polyval in the resolved graph. Neither covers argon2 (own `zeroize` feature pinned; memory and key wrapped in `Zeroizing`, crypto.rs:71-81), the nonce and tag (not secret, stack copies at :109-110 unwiped), nor aes-gcm's stack `mask` block (upstream, unwiped).

Pre-existing and unchanged in the range: `encrypt_in_place` calls `try_reserve_exact(GCM_TAG_BYTES)` on the plaintext `Zeroizing<Vec<u8>>` (crypto.rs:90-92); when the caller's Vec has no spare capacity (the WIT lift path) the buffer is reallocated and the old plaintext allocation is freed without wiping — `Zeroizing` wipes only the final buffer. Native builds of aes 0.9.3 select AES-NI/ARMv8 at runtime through cpufeatures with the fixslice as fallback; the assertions in crypto.rs are wasm32-scoped by design, so a native host without AES instructions would silently run the 64-bit fixslice — acceptable (constant-time either way) and irrelevant to the qualified artifact, which is wasm32 only.
